title: Engagement Initiation - Padstone Sprint Outline
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc frames the initial 4-week technical sprint to validate Padstone's major product hypothesis: a near-real-time assistant for their analytics dashboard powered by open LLMs running on Redwood’s inference stack. This is a working engagement plan — lightweight, deliberately iterative.

Quick summary (elevator):
- Goal: Prove Padstone can serve interactive natural-language queries over private product telemetry with acceptable latency and cost using Redwood Hosted -> Dedicated fallbacks.
- Duration: 4 weeks (2 x focused sprints + 1 buffer week + 1 tie-off week)
- Primary success signals: 95th percentile generation latency < 200ms for baseline prompts in our test harness; semantic answer precision >= 88% on the curated eval set; demonstrable end-to-end privacy posture for PII-containing telemetry.

Scope (in-scope):
- Integration: prototype a request path from Padstone frontend -> Redwood API -> model variant -> response rendering.
- Evals: build 150-prompt evaluation suite reflecting production traffic patterns (mix of short/long context, retrieval-augmented queries).
- Deployment modes: exercise Hosted API and a Dedicated pool (small reserved capacity) to compare latency and cost.
- Observability: wire traces and token-level cost breakdown into Redwood Console and Padstone’s Sentry/Datadog.
- Data handling: test retrieval and redaction middleware for PII in telemetry.

Non-goals (out-of-scope this sprint):
- Full Private (VPC) installation or on-prem air-gapped deployment — we will capture requirements for a follow-on dedicated phase.
- Deep model training or RLHF — we will only use off-the-shelf open models + quantized variants.
- UI polish or productized SDKs — the front-end will be a simple iframe demo or dev console only.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Padstone (customer):
  - Product sponsor: Claire Montoya (Padstone)
  - Engineering lead: Samir Khan (Padstone)
- Redwood:
  - Engagement lead / owner: Aisha Patel (solutions-engineering)
  - Runtime SME: Kenji Watanabe (serving-runtime)
  - Privacy & Security: Lina Morales (security-and-compliance)
  - Observability: Tomás Alvarez (observability)
  - Solutions engineer: Priya Menon (solutions-engineering)

Week-by-week plan (high level):
- Week 0 (pre-sprint, 3 days): alignment workshop, Slack channel created, minimal access exchange (API keys, test dataset).
- Week 1: quick integration + baseline run on Hosted API. Deliverable: baseline harness results, sample traces.
- Week 2: deploy dedicated small pool, tune batching/kv-cache strategy, run comparative load tests. Deliverable: Dedicated vs Hosted report.
- Week 3: privacy validation, retrieval integration (RAG), refine eval set and rerun metrics. Deliverable: privacy checklist and eval report.
- Week 4 (tie-off): stakeholder demo, handoff notes, decision doc (go/no-go + recommended next steps).

Deliverables (artifact list):
- integration-checklist.md (simple runbook for enabling host <-> customer test path)
- padstone-eval-suite.csv (150 prompts, expected outputs, severity tags)
- perf-comparison.pdf (Hosted vs Dedicated latency/cost/throughput)
- privacy-validation.txt (redaction tests, KMS usage notes)
- rollout-recommendation.md (next-step options: reserved capacity, VPC assessment, SLO targets)

Success criteria (explicit and measurable):
- Quantitative (hard pass/fail rules):
  1) Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and <= 400ms for long prompts (>=512 tokens) under baseline traffic (10 qps sustained).
  2) Quality: semantic-accuracy on eval set (operationalized via binary judgment) >= 88% and no rollout-blocking regressions vs baseline model.
  3) Cost: steady-state token cost (model + infra) <= $0.75 per 1k tokens for targeted deployment (projected).
  4) Reliability: end-to-end success (no errors) >= 99.5% during a 30 minute stress window.
  5) Data controls: PII redaction test coverage = 100% for injected PII tokens in telemetry examples.
- Qualitative (stakeholder readiness):
  - Padstone product team can reproduce the demo with internal devs and understands tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted.
  - Security sign-off: Lina confirms no blocker in the privacy posture for the minimal dataset used in the sprint.

Evaluation methodology:
- Use the padstone-eval-suite.csv and an automated grader harness (github link above) to classify outputs into correct/acceptable/unacceptable. Manual spot-checks for edge cases.
- Traffic shaping: replay production-like trace sample (provided by Padstone) at 10 qps and a 60 qps spike to observe degradation/fallback behavior.
- Cost model: capture token counts and instance-hours, run through Redwood’s cost estimator to produce projected $/1k-token numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated.

Key technical risks & mitigation: 
- Risk: KV cache warming could cause initial high latency on cold start.
  - Mitigation: pre-warm with representative prefixes, measure cold vs warm latency and capture in report.
- Risk: Retrieval layer increase context length and memory pressure.
  - Mitigation: cap retrieved docs per-query and test quantized model variant for memory savings.
- Risk: PII leakage in middle-layer logs.
  - Mitigation: enable redact-on-write middleware, limit retention, use KMS-protected logs where possible, test with synthetic PII.

Workshop agenda (90 minutes alignment session — Week 0):
- 00:00–00:10: Introductions + success definition (Aisha / Claire)
- 00:10–00:25: Product demo and target user flows (Samir)
- 00:25–00:40: Architecture & data flow review (Kenji + Lina)
- 00:40–00:55: Eval plan and metrics (Tomás)
- 00:55–01:05: Deployment options / constraints (Priya)
- 01:05–01:20: Risks, open questions, and data access checklist (group)
- 01:20–01:30: Immediate next steps & meeting cadence (Aisha)

Open questions (to resolve during Week 0):
- What subset of telemetry is safe for testing (fields + retention)? Padstone to provide white-listed schema.
- Will Padstone accept synthetic telemetry for privacy-sensitive endpoints?
- Expected production qps and peak concurrency numbers for capacity planning.
- Any network egress constraints if we later move to VPC/private deployment?

Acceptance / exit criteria for this sprint (decision gate):
- A formal decision document signed by Claire and Aisha indicating one of: move-to-reserved (book Dedicated capacity), plan-VPC-assessment (schedule follow-on), or iterate (additional 2-week spike).
- The perf-comparison.pdf shows no hard blocker for 95th percentile latency targets OR a clear, actionable mitigation plan with cost/impact analysis.

Temporary notes / runbook fragments (quick wins):
- When testing Hosted, enable streaming responses to keep frontend latency under 120ms perceived for short turns.
- Use token-level tracing in Redwood Console to map expensive prompts to model kernels / batch sizes.
- Try a half-quantized int8 variant for memory savings before moving to full int4 — watch for hallucination increase.

Communication plan:
- Weekly syncs: Tuesdays 10am PT (internal padstone-redwood engineers).
- Demo + stakeholder review: final Friday of sprint 4 at 1pm PT.
- Slack: #ps-padstone-engagement (redwood) + padstone private channel for execs with read-only artifacts.

Appendix: quick checklist for Week 1 integration
- [ ] Exchange API key + debug token (Padstone -> Redwood)
- [ ] Provide sample telemetry xform rules + schema (Padstone)
- [ ] Redwood: provision test Dedicated pool (small) for Week 2
- [ ] Create padstone-eval-suite.csv draft (Aisha + Priya)
- [ ] Set up perf harness and baseline job (Kenji)

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep the eval set starved of product names to test generalization.
- Prioritize an early demo that shows latency numbers in the console; visuals help speed up exec buy-in.

-- end of working draft --

Unresolved (placeholders to fill in after Week 0):
- exact billing contact for Padstone to attach Dedicated invoice
- final list of allowed telemetry fields
- preferred Slack time for quick escalations (default: 9am PT)
